openings.claim: The incumbent may depend on reliably seating corner contacts before clamp closure; visually tight closure does not establish that seating.
openings.delta: Change only the hand-operation order: deliberate stop-and-corner seating before tightening versus tightening without deliberate corner seating. Keep the incumbent geometry and materials.
openings.prediction: Deliberate seating should reduce unloaded return scatter if inconsistent contact is dominant. The nearest rival is pocket or connection flexibility: similar unloaded returns but displacement during load would favor that rival. Similar scatter under both actions defeats the seating explanation; both mechanisms may coexist.
openings.probe: First check the incumbent fits the envelope, retains every component and permits hand exchange with available hardware. If fabricable within 100 minutes, use one configuration for five exchanges of each rod, alternating operation orders within each position; replace the 19 mm rod with 18 mm for its last two exchanges. Record unloaded return, exchange time and four distributed ten-second 10 N loads, two per operation order. Allow up to two repeat exchanges within the twelve-exchange cap. Any constraint breach or outcome failure rejects that tested sequence. Twenty minutes must cover exchange, loading and logging; insufficient time or unequal seating access makes attribution inconclusive. This is a probe, not deployment.
assumptions: Shared-fastener geometry can be assembled from eight bolts and six plywood pieces.
Ruler and target card resolve meaningful return differences; ten mixed exchanges provide weak attribution.

assessment: Two incumbent dependencies remain unverified: seating consistency and hardware/connection capacity. A stop alone proves neither an informative test nor success.

lineage.reason: Keep the incumbent as the test object while narrowing its performance claim to a seating-versus-flexibility challenge.

attacks.dependency: Eight bolts can connect, stop and clamp both pockets rigidly while captive. No allocation or stiffness evidence is supplied; fabrication and initial load checks may defeat feasibility before comparison.
